Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1516 and H2011); valley of (the son of) Hinnom; ge-henna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment:--hell.
BiblicalUsage: géenna means hell. It occurs 12 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Matthew, Mark, Luke, and James — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe géenna matters because judgment is real, and so is the mercy that saves us from it. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
